transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need. It's probably just regular stress—I'm a tax preparer, so things can get a bit hectic—but I guess what brings me in is that I keep having these... well, these strange moments. 

I feel a little silly even saying it out loud, because I really don't want to sound crazy or anything, but lately, my own house or my office will just suddenly feel completely unreal. It's almost like... like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it the right way for you.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself or as though the world around you isn't real, even when you're not having these sudden moments you described?

Oh, no, definitely not. I'm sorry if I made it sound like that. Most of the time, I'm... I'm just regular old me, you know? Just doing my work and going about my day. 

It's really just those specific, sudden flashes where things get kind of... weird. Between those moments, everything feels completely normal and real, I promise. I hope that's a good sign? I really don't want to make this sound worse than it actually is, and I'm definitely still functioning fine the rest of the time. Is that... is that helpful to know?

When you're having one of these sudden moments, do you ever feel detached from yourself, as if you're observing your own body from the outside, or does the world around you feel like a dream or a movie?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, I hope I didn't make it sound too dramatic earlier. I wouldn't really say the world feels like a movie or a dream, no. I haven't really noticed anything quite like that. 

It's mostly just... well, just that weird feeling I mentioned before, where it's like I'm suddenly standing across the room looking at myself sitting at my desk. But even when that happens, I know I'm still me, you know? I don't want you to think I'm totally losing touch with reality or anything. It's probably just my brain being a little overworked from tax season. 

Does that... does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
During these sudden moments, does the environment around you ever feel unreal, like it's distorted, foggy, or not quite there—even if just slightly?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really haven't noticed anything like that. The room itself always looks completely normal, you know? The walls, the desk, everything is right where it should be. It doesn't get blurry or foggy or anything weird like that. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm not making this too confusing for you. I know I said it feels strange, but the actual room around me is totally fine. It's really just that brief, weird feeling of kind of... seeing myself from the corner. But the environment is perfectly normal, I promise. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.
Outside of those sudden moments, have you ever felt like you or the world around you seemed unreal, even slightly or briefly?

Oh, um, no. I'm so sorry, I must not have explained myself very well earlier, and I feel terrible if I'm making you ask the same things over again! But really, outside of those little flashes, everything is completely, one hundred percent normal. 

I definitely don't walk around feeling like things are fake or anything like that. When I'm just going about my day, working on my clients' tax returns, I'm completely grounded and... well, just me. I promise I'm not losing my grip on things overall. I hope that clears it up a bit? I really want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Between those sudden moments, have you ever felt like you were detached from your body or that parts of your body felt unreal or unfamiliar, even slightly?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I'm so sorry if I've been giving you the wrong impression with all of this. I really don't want you to think there's something seriously wrong with me, you know? 

Between those little weird moments, I feel completely connected to my body. My hands are my hands, my feet are my feet... nothing feels strange or unfamiliar at all. I'm just a regular guy sitting at a desk crunching numbers, I promise. Everything is totally normal in between. 

I hope I'm answering these questions right for you? I just really want to make sure I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it actually is.
Between those sudden moments, have you ever felt like your thoughts or emotions didn’t belong to you or felt disconnected from them, even just a little?

No, no, not at all. My thoughts are definitely my own. I mean, I might get a little stressed about deadlines—tax season is right around the corner, you know—but I've never felt disconnected from my own mind or my feelings. 

I'm really sorry, I feel like I keep giving you "no" answers, and I hope you don't think I'm being difficult or hiding anything from you. I just want to be as honest and helpful as I can. But yeah, my thoughts and emotions are completely normal and they definitely belong to me. Is that... is that okay? Am I giving you the right kind of information?
During those sudden moments, do you ever notice physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, shaking, or trouble catching your breath?

Oh, um... no. I really don't think so. My heart doesn't race, and I'm definitely not shaking or sweating or... or having trouble breathing. I mean, maybe I get just a tiny bit tense, like anyone would when they're startled, but physically, I'm completely fine. 

I'm so sorry, I feel terrible that I keep shooting down your questions! I really hope it's okay that I keep saying no. I just want to be as accurate as possible for you so you have exactly what you need. It's really just those little flashes in my head, nothing physical like that. 

I hope... I hope that's a good thing? That I don't have those physical symptoms, I mean. Am I still giving you helpful answers?
